sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an $8.3 billion impairment charge, mostly a $6.8 billion Shave Care goodwill write-down [F13][D97][X109][X112][P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% to $15.7 billion as $8.3 billion of the increase came from the base-period impairment charge [F14][D148][P71].
Since then the shape is slow compounding: revenue grew 2.0% a year over FY2023 to FY2026, and operating margin has held between 22.1% and 24.3% [D664][F27][F29].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +4.0pp of FY2020 revenue growth and +2.2pp in FY2024 [D518][D530].
In FY2026 the pattern flipped: Non-US contributed +3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added just +0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added +0.8pp in FY2026, while Beauty added +1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D541][D543][D603][D602].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, so there was no operating leverage, and operating income fell 3.4% [D482][D458].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits 0.6pp above the 22.1% window median but 1.6pp below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][D647][D470].
The FY2026 decline came from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp), as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and SG&A rose on marketing spending [D483][D485][P5].
Net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, with the gap driven by interest and tax rather than operating items [F50][F30][D693].
The effective tax rate rose to 20.8% from 20.3% on lower excess tax benefits from share-based compensation and unfavorable geographic mix [D443][D392][P23].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, above the 1.25x window median only marginally below it, and free cash flow was 0.94x net income [F80][F40][D444][D683][D445].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, while inventories consumed $641 million on higher safety stock [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is in line with the 17.2% window median, and capex at 5.1% of revenue was 1.40x D&A [D441][D654][D440][D446].
Investing cash use rose to $4.6 billion, primarily capital expenditures and settlement of net investment hedges [F110][P2].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, or net cash of -27.8% of revenue, against a staples peer median of -19.2% on the same basis (n=3) [D450][D451][D695].
That places it at the 67th percentile for net cash, and the current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median [D694][F180][D663].
Buybacks plus dividends of $15.3 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D452][D453][D476].
Payout has exceeded free cash flow in most years of the window, so the dividend and buyback are funded partly by balance-sheet capacity rather than cash generation alone [D402][D453].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window and stood at 0.68x in FY2026, with current liabilities of $38.7 billion against current assets of $26.2 billion [R1][F180][F160][F150].
This is structural for a consumer staples company with steady cash generation, but it leaves little liquidity cushion if refinancing conditions tighten [R1].
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% respectively [R2][D402][D453].
The gap is small in FY2026 and covered by cash on hand, but a repeat of the FY2025 shortfall would force either slower buybacks or more debt [R2].
Whether operating margin holds above the 22.1% window median in the FY2027 10-K, after the 1.6pp decline to 22.7% in FY2026 [D648][F30][D470].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 20.5% FY2021 high from 17.4% in FY2026, as capex has risen to 5.1% of revenue [D653][D441][D440].
Whether the current ratio moves back above the 0.72x window median from 0.68x, given current liabilities grew 7.3% in FY2026 [D663][F180][D469].
